summary: All four machine-readable specs (platform-architecture.json, tenant-model.json, cedar-fragment-schema.json, compliance-pack-schema.json) parse as valid JSON (verified via `python3 -m json`). The three schema specs correctly declare `$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` and exercise Draft 2020-12 idioms appropriately (`if`/`then` in `allOf`, `uniqueItems`, `pattern`, `format: date-time`/`email`, `additionalProperties`, `minLength`/`maxLength`, `minItems`, conditional schemas). All inline regex `pattern` strings compile under ECMA-262 / Python `re` semantics (validated against semver, ISO-3166, BCP 47-like, ISO-8601 duration, SHA-256 hex, Ed25519 hex-128, semver-range slices). Cedar v4.2 fragment frontmatter shape is consistent with the AWS Cedar OOPSLA-2024 LTS surface (Entity::Action::"Name" form, scoped fragments, signed envelope, deny-wins composition). Postgres DDL excerpts in ADR-0246 (policy_engine.fragments + signatures + signing_keys + coverage_reports + evaluation_audit_index + bootstrap_genesis) and ADR-0249 (listings, listing_categories, listing_media, inventory_records/transactions/reservations) and ADR-0257 (schema_revision_registry + _consumer_pin + _consumer_acknowledgement + _dual_write_window) are syntactically valid Postgres-14+ DDL with consistent column types (TEXT/UUID/JSONB/TIMESTAMPTZ/BYTEA/INTEGER/NUMERIC), proper CHECK constraints, REFERENCES with ON DELETE policy, GIN/B-tree indexes, RLS (ENABLE + FORCE) with tenant-isolation policies, GENERATED ALWAYS AS for derived columns. The schema-revision versioning rules per ADR-0257 §D-1 (SemVer 2.0.0 strict, pre-release + build metadata) match the canonical semver.org BNF. Two MINOR findings flag (1) the cedar-fragment-schema's `signature` field carries a `minLength`+`maxLength`=128 plus pattern `^[0-9a-f]+$`; the compliance-pack-schema's equivalent uses tighter `^[0-9a-f]{128}$` — same effect but inconsistent style across two co-bundled schemas, and (2) the cedar-fragment-schema's `scope` pattern accepts overlay jurisdiction codes as `[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,8})?` while tenant-model.json's `jurisdiction.primary` uses `[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?` — sub-region suffix max-length disagrees by 5 chars between sibling specs. Neither finding rises to a fail; both are recommended-fix-before-promote-to-BLOCKER items.

findings: Correct use of Draft-2020-12 conditional `allOf`/`if`/`then` shape for cross-field constraints (PLATFORM_OWNER => reserved-namespace tenant_id; SANDBOX/PREVIEW => kyc_status const; can_settle => merchant_status enum + tax_registrations.minItems).

tenant_id regex `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?){0,5}$` enforces sub-scope depth=4 with root in addition (total 5 segments per `{0,5}` after the root) — aligns with platform-architecture.json `max_sub_scope_depth: 4`.

Custom `x-enum-descriptions`, `x-reserved-namespace-check`, `x-max-sub-scope-depth`, `x-reserved-namespace-validation`, `x-reserved-namespace-roots` annotations use the conventional `x-` prefix per JSON Schema vendor-extension idiom (compatible with Draft 2020-12).
`pattern` for ISO 3166-2 jurisdiction uses `^[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?$` — note divergence with cedar-fragment-schema overlay pattern (`{1,8}`); see recommendations.
DSAR `response_sla_days` enforced via min 1 / max 90; appropriate per GDPR Art. 12 default 30.
Cedar action names per `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*::Action::"[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*"$` match Cedar v4.2 grammar (EntityType::Action::"Identifier").
Resource type pattern `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$` matches Cedar Entity Type BNF.

Fragment `scope` enum tokens (`baseline|pack/<id>|overlay/<jur>|reserved|tenant/<id>`) match ADR-0246 §scope_directory_layout; pack-id regex `[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]` aligns with compliance-pack-schema's pack_id `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(-[A-Za-z0-9.]+)*$` modulo case (cedar fragment requires uppercase, pack-schema permits leading lower — see recommendations).
Ed25519 signature pattern uses `^[0-9a-f]+$` + minLength=maxLength=128. Functionally identical to `^[0-9a-f]{128}$` (used in compliance-pack-schema) — style inconsistency noted.

`allOf` conditional rules (reserved => coverage_role=default-deny; pack/ => signed_by=pack-owner:; overlay/ => signed_by=overlay-owner:; tenant/ => signed_by=tenant-admin:; incident-response: => sunset_at required) implement ADR-0243 §D-2/§D-11 invariants schematically.

Cedar fragment samples in ADR-0247 (§D-8 self-modification permit/forbid for Workflow::Action, Cedar::Action, Substrate::Action) and ADR-0243 §D-4 messenger permit are well-formed Cedar v4.2 (proper `permit (...) when {...}`, `forbid (...) when {...}` syntax, action lists, resource `is` guards).
Cosign attestation reference pattern `^(rekor|seaweed)://[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+@[0-9a-f]{64}$` enforces SHA-256 hex digest = exactly 64 hex chars; matches Sigstore Rekor + SeaweedFS conventions.

per_adr_findings.adr: ADR-0246 (policy-engine substrate DDL embedded in ADR text)
findings: policy_engine.fragments DDL uses CHECK constraint on activation_status enum (`AUTHORED|REVIEWED|SIGNED|PUBLISHED|ACTIVE|SUNSET|TOMBSTONED`) — matches ADR-0246 §lifecycle states verbatim.
GIN index on applies_to_actions array column appropriate for action-array containment queries; B-tree composite index on (effective_at, sunset_at) supports temporal window queries.
Foreign key REFERENCES policy_engine.fragments(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT correctly forbids cascade-delete of signed fragments (audit retention invariant).

Signing keys table uses self-referential parent_key_id REFERENCES signing_keys(key_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT and CHECK on key_type enum + revocation_status enum + quorum_required range [1,9] — all valid.
coverage_reports table uses NUMERIC(5,4) GENERATED ALWAYS AS (covered_count::numeric / NULLIF(action_count,0)) STORED — valid Postgres 12+ syntax (assumed; see recommendation).
evaluation_audit_index decision CHECK (`PERMIT|FORBID|NOT_APPLICABLE`) matches Cedar v4.2 decision enum exactly.
listings PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, listing_id) supports Citus shard-key colocation per platform-architecture.json data_substrate doctrine.
JSONB GIN indexes on attributes + search_keywords appropriate for category-specific attribute query.

FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, listing_id) REFERENCES listings(tenant_id, listing_id) ON DELETE CASCADE in listing_attributes — composite FK valid; ON DELETE CASCADE acceptable for owned-collection semantics (vs ON DELETE RESTRICT used for audit-bound fragments).
Inventory CHECK constraints (available_qty >= 0, reserved_qty >= 0, quantity > 0) enforce non-negative inventory invariants at the DDL layer; correct.
listing_state_transitions uses gen_random_uuid() default — requires pgcrypto extension (assumed loaded; not a defect of the DDL itself).

ISO 8601 duration pattern `^P(?:[0-9]+Y)?(?:[0-9]+M)?(?:[0-9]+W)?(?:[0-9]+D)?(?:T(?:[0-9]+H)?(?:[0-9]+M)?(?:[0-9]+S)?)?$` is correct per ISO 8601-1:2019; matches retention_min, max_duration_iso8601, tamper_detection_frequency.
Pack-id pattern `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(-[A-Za-z0-9.]+)*$` allows examples like `HIPAA-2024`, `PCI-DSS-L1-v4`, `KR-PIPA-2023-amendment` — valid.
data_class_extensions pattern `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` (UPPER_SNAKE) — matches ADR-0099 data-class registry naming convention.

Cell-eligibility forbidden_cells supports glob patterns (`data-plane-cn-*`, `data-plane-ru-*`); the schema declares them as plain strings (no regex enforcement) — relies on consumer-side glob interpretation; acceptable for free-form patterns.

consent_requirements.purpose_consent_types enum (13 values incl. `health-data-processing`, `automated-decision-making`, `international-transfer`, `minor-data-processing`) is comprehensive for GDPR/HIPAA/KR-PIPA/EU-AI-Act coverage.

jurisdiction_overlay pattern `^(\*|[A-Z]{2,3}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?)$` accepts ISO 3166-1 alpha-2/alpha-3 + sub-national + wildcard — note `{2,3}` permits alpha-3 codes which tenant-model.json does NOT (it only accepts alpha-2); see recommendations.
schema_revision_registry CHECK (lifecycle_state IN ('ACTIVE','DEPRECATED','TOMBSTONED')) matches §D-3 state machine exactly.
Composite PRIMARY KEY (object_type_name, schema_revision) is appropriate (one revision per object type).
Partial index `WHERE lifecycle_state = 'ACTIVE'` and `WHERE lifecycle_state = 'DEPRECATED'` correctly uses Postgres partial index for hot-path lookup.
RLS policy via current_setting('app.tenant_id') is the Postgres-canonical multi-tenant isolation pattern; ENABLE + FORCE pair prevents superuser bypass (correct).

Denormalised semver columns (major/minor/patch) + JSONB schema_definition_canonical_json + BYTEA schema_definition_hash + BYTEA ed25519_signature — types align with `feedback_no_silent_regression` provenance requirements.

schema_revision SemVer BNF in §D-1 mirrors semver.org §2-§11 verbatim (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH + optional `-PRERELEASE` + optional `+BUILDMETA`); invalid examples (`1.0`, `v1.0.0`, `2026-05-20`, `1.0.0_rc1`) correctly rejected.

Cedar fragment in §D-8 (`permit (...) when { resource.object_type_schema_revision in principal.tenant.allowed_schema_revisions[resource.object_type] && resource.object_type_schema_revision_lifecycle == "ACTIVE" };`) is well-formed Cedar v4.2; uses `in` set membership + map index + string equality — all v4.2 supported.

Annotation syntax `annotation header "X-Ontology-Schema-Deprecated"` is non-standard Cedar v4.2 (Cedar v4.2 supports `@annotation` directives but the header-translation pattern shown is conceptual; this is acknowledged as 'modeled here as a permit with an annotation that the gateway translates' — interpretation-level only, not a real Cedar primitive). Documented as conceptual; not a defect, but worth a line of clarification before lane promotion.

openapi_version_compliance.notes: The four corpus specs are JSON Schema documents, not OpenAPI documents. OpenAPI 3.2.0 compliance is enforced elsewhere (per-microservice contracts/openapi/*.yaml per ADR-0245 + planned_contracts/ per build-ahead-of-certification doctrine). No OpenAPI fragments in the A6 corpus to validate.
openapi_version_compliance.indirect_signal: platform-architecture.json §microservice_taxonomy.manifest_schema_ref points at /specs/per-microservice-flat-layout.json (out of A6 corpus scope); §certification_gates references `planned_contracts/openapi/*.yaml` consistently with ADR-0250.

asyncapi_version_compliance.notes: AsyncAPI 3.1.0 compliance is enforced at per-microservice contracts/asyncapi/*.yaml level (per ADR-0145 inter-microservice communication reform). ADR-0257 §D-5 declares the `ObjectTypeSchemaEvolved` event topic `ontology.schema-evolution.v1` with seven subtypes (Registered, MinorBumped, PatchBumped, Deprecated, Tombstoned, ConsumerAcknowledged, GracePeriodExtended) — the prose schema is well-defined but no AsyncAPI YAML is materialised in the corpus, so direct AsyncAPI 3.1.0 validation is deferred to the per-microservice contract files.

checks_performed: CHECK constraint enum membership matches lifecycle/state enums declared in JSON schemas
REFERENCES with ON DELETE policy specified (RESTRICT for audit-bound, CASCADE for owned-collection)
PRIMARY KEY composition supports Citus shard colocation per data_substrate doctrine
Index types appropriate (GIN for JSONB/arrays, partial WHERE for state-filtered lookup, B-tree composite for temporal/key-lookup)
RLS ENABLE + FORCE pair on every tenant-scoped table
GENERATED ALWAYS AS for derived columns (coverage_ratio in ADR-0246)
TIMESTAMPTZ used uniformly (no naive TIMESTAMP)
BYTEA for cryptographic primitives (signatures, hashes, key material)
JSONB for semi-structured payloads (annotations, attributes, schema_definition_canonical_json, breaking_changes_json)
TEXT for semver strings (vs custom domain) — acceptable given semver validation lives in domain layer
Statement shape `permit/forbid (principal, action, resource) when {...}` matches Cedar v4.2 grammar
Entity::Action::"Name" form used consistently
`resource is EntityType` guards used correctly
Action lists `action in [Action1, Action2, ...]` syntactically valid
Operator usage (`==`, `!=`, `in`, `matches`, `contains`, `&&`, `||`, `!`) all v4.2 supported
String literals correctly double-quoted with escape handling

Composition semantics declared in platform-architecture.json §policy.composition_semantics (permits_union, forbids_override_permits, deny_wins_ties, not_applicable_default) match Cedar v4.2 deny-wins semantics
cedar_v4_2_syntax_validity.minor_observation: ADR-0257 §D-8 uses a conceptual `annotation header "X-Ontology-Schema-Deprecated"` to model deprecation warning response headers — this is documented as 'modeled here as a permit with an annotation that the gateway translates into a response header'. Real Cedar v4.2 supports `@annotation(...)` directives on policies but not response-header translation natively; the ADR's framing is correct (conceptual mapping, not a literal Cedar primitive). Not a defect.

checks_performed: All four corpus JSON files parse as syntactically valid JSON (python3 json.load verified)
All three schema specs declare $schema = https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
$id declared with stable canonical URI per Draft 2020-12 §8
type/required/properties tripartite shape used uniformly on object schemas
Conditional schema composition via allOf+if+then (Draft 2020-12 §10.2.2) used correctly
x-vendor-extension annotations used per JSON Schema convention
All inline regex patterns compile under ECMA-262 syntax (semver, ISO-3166, ISO-8601 duration, SHA-256, semver-range slices, BCP-47-like tokens)
format specifiers (date-time, email) within Draft 2020-12 vocabulary
Enum + minItems + uniqueItems + minLength/maxLength constraints applied appropriately

recommendations.title: Harmonise Ed25519 signature regex style across cedar-fragment-schema.json and compliance-pack-schema.json
recommendations.recommended: Both adopt `^[0-9a-f]{128}$` (tighter; one source of truth; reads as documentation)
recommendations.blocker_for: BLOCKER promotion of oya gate validate cedar-fragment-signature lane

recommendations.title: Reconcile ISO 3166-2 sub-region suffix length across specs
recommendations.current: tenant-model.json jurisdiction.primary: `^[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?$` (max 3 chars after dash) vs cedar-fragment-schema.json overlay scope: `^overlay/[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,8})?$` (max 8) vs compliance-pack-schema.json jurisdiction_overlay: `^[A-Z]{2,3}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?$` (alpha-2 OR alpha-3 + max 3 sub-suffix)
recommendations.recommended: Standardise on ISO 3166-2 official spec: alpha-2 country + dash + 1..3 alphanumeric sub-region code (`[A-Z]{2}(-[A-Z0-9]{1,3})?`). Permit alpha-3 only in compliance-pack jurisdiction_overlay if there is a regulator-cited rationale (e.g., GBR for UK in some regulator filings); document the exception.
recommendations.blocker_for: BLOCKER promotion of oya gate validate cellular-blast-radius-bounding + sovereign-cloud-overlay lanes

recommendations.title: Reconcile pack-id case convention
recommendations.current: cedar-fragment-schema scope pack-id segment: `pack/[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]` (UPPER) vs compliance-pack-schema pack_id: `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(-[A-Za-z0-9.]+)*$` (mixed case + dots permitted)
recommendations.recommended: Compliance-pack-schema is authoritative (binding ADR is ADR-0251); narrow cedar-fragment-schema scope pattern to mirror the same pack_id regex OR document the case-fold convention explicitly. Sample data uses UPPER (`HIPAA-2024`, `PCI-DSS-L1-v4`), so tightening to UPPER would align both.
recommendations.blocker_for: BLOCKER promotion of oya gate validate pack-cell-certification-coherence lane

recommendations.title: Clarify the conceptual Cedar `annotation header` syntax in ADR-0257 §D-8
recommendations.current: Reads as a Cedar primitive but is described in prose as 'modeled here as a permit with an annotation that the gateway translates into a response header'
recommendations.recommended: Replace the embedded `annotation header "X-..."` lines with a code comment or a separate prose paragraph that makes clear the gateway-level translation. Avoids reviewer confusion that the syntax is a real v4.2 primitive.

recommendations.title: Add explicit AsyncAPI 3.1.0 source for ObjectTypeSchemaEvolved event family
recommendations.current: ADR-0257 §D-5 declares topic + subtype matrix in Markdown table; no asyncapi.yaml fragment materialised in corpus
recommendations.recommended: Produce microservices/ontology/contracts/asyncapi/ontology-schema-evolution.v1.yaml before ADR-0257 promotes from advisory to BLOCKER. Will allow A6-Schema lane to mechanically validate AsyncAPI 3.1.0 conformance.
recommendations.blocker_for: BLOCKER promotion of oya gate validate schema-evolution-event-emitted lane

recommendations.title: Postgres pgcrypto extension prerequisite for gen_random_uuid() should be declared in migration prelude
recommendations.current: ADR-0249 DDL uses gen_random_uuid() default; ADR-0257 worker emits UUIDs but its DDL uses TEXT for HLC timestamps — no immediate pgcrypto dep
recommendations.recommended: Per-microservice 0000_extensions.sql migration that issues `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;` to make the dependency self-contained for fresh-cell bootstrap.

overall_signal_for_synthesizer.rationale: Schema-side substrate of the keystone bundle is solid. Postgres DDL is Postgres-14+ valid with correct tenant-isolation, type usage, and constraint hygiene across three ADRs (0246/0249/0257). JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 used correctly across three machine-readable specs with valid regex and idiomatic conditional composition. Cedar v4.2 fragments parse cleanly. SemVer 2.0.0 strict semantics in ADR-0257 §D-1 align with semver.org BNF. Three minor inter-spec consistency findings (R1-R3) are mechanical to fix and do not affect doctrine correctness; they should be cleaned up before A6 CI lanes flip to BLOCKER but do not gate this bundle's PROPOSED acceptance.
